The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) was filed in respect of the injuries sustained by the petitioner Shayara in a motor vehicular accident occurred within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal.

____________________________________________________________ 2. Briefly stated, the facts as emerged from the DAR are that on 23.05.2023 at about 08:00 p.m., the petitioner Shayara while coming home at Nathu Colony, Shahdara from her office at Babarpur,
Shahdara, alighted from an auto-rickshaw Flyover of Nathu Colony Chowk and after ensuring that no one was coming, started crossing the road.

Suddenly, a motorcycle bearing no. UP14EX-9313 (hereinafter, 'offending vehicle') being driven by its driver at a high speed and carelessly, came from GTB Red Light side and hit her, due to which she fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
Public persons gathered and caught the driver of the offending vehicle but he succeeded in fleeing away, leaving the offending vehicle at the spot of the accident.
The injured/ petitioner was taken to GTB Hospital, where her MLC was prepared.

In connection with the accident, FIR no.131/2023, under sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS M.S. Park, Delhi.
During investigation, it was found out that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3.

After completion of the investigation, charge-sheet against the driver/ respondent no.1 was filed before the concerned court and the present DAR against the respondents was filed before this Tribunal, which has been treated as claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 on behalf of the injured/petitioner.

5. In the joint written-statement filed on behalf of respondents no.1 and 2, it is contended that the respondent no.1 was driving the alleged offending vehicle very carefully and it was the petitioner who was crossing the road without having proper attention.
And despite warning given to the petitioner in loud voice and by blowing the horn, she got hit by the alleged offending vehicle.
It is stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured by the respondent no.3/ insurance company.

It is stated that the petitioner had called her associates at the spot of accident and they gave beatings to the respondent no.1 and falsely implicated him in the accident case, on which respondent no.1 made a call to police and got the FIR no. 132/2023 lodged at PS M.S. Park, under sections 323/341/506/34 IPC, seeking legal action against the persons who gave beatings to him.

Act also and the fact that driver/ respondent no.1 was not having a Driving License on the date of accident was well within the knowledge of owner/ insured and therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

Park, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. UP14EX-9313, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1
Whether

petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 13.05.2023 at about 08:00 p.m. at Nathu Colony Chowk Flyover, near stairs, within the jurisdiction of PS M.S. Park, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. UP14EX-9313, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver? OPP 12.
It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.

In the instant case, the happening of the present accident involving the offending vehicle being driven by the respondent no.1 is not in dispute, as this fact has been fairly admitted by the respondent no.1 and 2 in their joint written statement, however, it has been contended by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioner/ injured herself was responsible for causing the accident,
as she got hit by the offending vehicle because she was crossing the road without having proper attention and despite warning given to her in a loud voice and by blowing the horn.

Therefore, now what remains to be decided on this issue is if the driver/ respondent no.1 was driving the offending Shayara @ Sayra vs Deepanshu Verma on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83775087/
4 vehicle in rash and negligent manner, which resulting into the accident of the petitioner.

14. On this aspect, the petitioner (PW1) stated that when she reached over Nathu Colony Flyover just after the stairs, she left the auto- rickshaw and waited to cross the road when it is clear and when she found that there was no traffic on the road, she wished to cross the road but suddenly, a bike bearing registration number UP14EX-9313 came from GTB Hospital Red Light side at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit her, due to which she received injuries.
15.

unless and until, for one or the other reason, the vehicle has to halt in between.

Therefore, it does not matter in the present case whether the respondent no.1 was driving the offending motorcycle at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner; as the offending motorcycle would not have suddenly appeared at the spot of the accident to cause the accident with the petitioner.

The respondent no.1 would have been driving the offending motorcycle on the road, in whatever manner, immediately before the accident whether the petitioner saw or did not see the offending motorcycle.

16. It is deposed to by the petitioner in the affidavit of her evidence Ex.PW1/A that after leaving the auto-rickshaw, the she waited to cross the road when the road would have become clear and when the she found that there was no traffic/ vehicle on the road and she wished to cross the road, then suddenly the offending motorcycle came from the side of GTB Red Light signal.

From the site plan as well as the photograph of the road/ flyover, which is part of DAR, the place where the accident happened, it is apparent that if before crossing the road the petitioner would have seen on both sides of the road immediately before crossing the road, even if the speed of the offending motorcycle would have been excessively high, the petitioner would have seen the offending motorcycle from the direction from where the offending motorcycle was coming.

The fact that the petitioner was hit by offending motorcycle indicates that the petitioner has lied in examination-in-chief regarding the fact that the ____________________________________________________________ petitioner, after finding that there was no traffic/ vehicle on the road, the petitioner tried to cross the road.

17. It is further deposed to by the petitioner in her affidavit Ex.PW1/A that after the accident, she was blacked out for a few minutes and fell on the road and the respondent no.1 along with the offending motorcycle also fell on the road.

Someone from the passerby picked the petitioner and made her sit on the side of the road and when the respondent no.1 tried to escape from the spot,
someone from the passerby caught the respondent no.1 as well as the offending motorcycle.
On these facts, there has been no effective cross- examination on behalf of the respondent no.1 and 2 and as such, these facts are more or so unrebutted and would have to be believed to be true.
18. The respondent no.1 i.e. driver of the offending motorcycle, namely Deepanshu Verma has been examined as a defence witness.

In his affidavit of examination exhibited as R2W1/X, it is deposed to that the claim petition of the petitioner is not maintainable, as the petitioner had crossed the road in Shayara @ Sayra vs Deepanshu Verma on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83775087/
5 negligent manner without looking for the vehicle and that the petitioner had hit another vehicle, as the attention of the petitioner was not towards the moving vehicle in her direction.

And that the petitioner was wearing ear buds/ bluetooth and in the process of saving herself from other vehicles,
it was the petitioner who had hit the offending motorcycle in the middle of the road despite the w a r n i n g g i v e n t o t h e p e t i t i o n e r i n l o u d v o i c e a n d b y ____________________________________________________________ horn by the driver of the offending motorcycle.

It is further deposed to that at the time of the accident, the petitioner made a call to her associates and they had reached at the spot of accident, where they started beating the driver of the offending motorcycle and threatened regarding his false implication.

That the call was made to the police on behalf of the respondents no.1 and 2 as well and on the basis of their complaint FIR no. 132/2023 under section 223/341/506/34 IPC had been registered at PS MS Park against the petitioner, her father and her two associates.
These facts are in contradiction to the facts as deposed to by the petitioner, which have been believed to be true by the Tribunal because of lack of effective cross-examination.
19. On behalf of the petitioner, the cross-examination of respondent no.1/ R1W1 consists of that, "it is correct that in the said accident my bike was involved.
It is correct that I was driving the motorbike."

The effect of such cross-examination is that the entire material facts whatever had been stated in the affidavit of evidence, which is the examination-in-chief of R1W1 i.e. the driver/
respondent no.1 have gone completely unrebutted and, therefore, have to be assumed as true.
20. The Tribunal has a peculiar situation before it because of the ineffective cross-examination of the petitioner and the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending motorcycle.
Be that as it may, a pedestrian is required to follow the traffic rules while crossing the road.

A busy road should be c r o s s e d b y a p e d e s t r i a n t h r o u g h z e b r a ____________________________________________________________ crossing only and that too after ensuring that no traffic is coming from either side.
21.
In the present case, the Site Plan already referred to hereinabove reveals that the road on which the accident occurred is a two-way road with divider in the middle.

The petitioner (PW1) in her cross- examination has shown her unawareness with respect to the existence of zebra crossing on the road where the accident happened, as she stated that "I cannot say there was zebra crossing".

Moreover, the Site Plan also does not show any zebra crossing on the road at the site of the accident,
which confirms the fact that petitioner was crossing the busy road on Nathu Colony Flyover without there being any zebra crossing.

The Site Plan further reveals that the petitioner had already crossed half of the road up to divider and the accident happened at the point when she just started to cross a further half portion of the road after divider.

It shows that the petitioner hastily started crossing the road after divider without ensuring that no vehicle was coming on the road, which shows her sheer negligence and the accident could have been avoided if she had been cautious in crossing the road.

Therefore, in the present scenario where the Tribunal has unrebutted testimony of the petitioner and the unrebutted testimony of the respondent no.1, the facts as deposed to by the respondent no.1 appear to be more probable than that of the petitioner.

ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
As the issue no.1 has been decided against the petitioner, it is held that the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.
Accordingly, issue no.2 is decided against the petitioner and in favour of the respondents.
24. The DAR/ claim petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
